Coordinators' Conclave-cum-Meeting of the Monitoring Committee for the First Year of Phase III (2025–30) under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative
articles.full_content:
The Coordinators' Conclave-cum-Meeting of the Monitoring Committee for the First Year of Phase III (2025–30) under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative was successfully organized by the CSIR-Human Resource Development Centre (CSIR-HRDC), Ghaziabad, in association with CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory (CSIR-NCL), Pune, on 06–07 August 2026 at CSIR-NCL, Pune. The two-day conclave served as a significant platform for reviewing the progress made during the first year of Phase III of the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative, facilitating knowledge exchange among participating laboratories, and strengthening collaborative efforts for the effective implementation of the programme.
The programme commenced with an inaugural session featuring the ceremonial welcome of dignitaries and participants, followed by the traditional lamp-lighting ceremony. Dr Rajesh G. Gonnade, Scientist-G, CSIR-NCL, welcomed the gathering and set the stage for the discussions by emphasizing the importance of collaboration, innovation and skill development in achieving the objectives of the meeting. Dr. Vinay Kumar, Scientist-G and Skill Nodal Principal Investigator, CSIR-HRDC, presented the objectives of the conclave and provided a brief overview of the remarkable progress achieved under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative during 2025–26. He highlighted the vision of CSIR integrated Skill Initiative’s pivotal role in creating a nationwide skill development ecosystem for nurturing industry-ready talent to build a technology-driven workforce. Dr. Abhishek Kumar, Scientist-F, CSIR-Central Planning Directorate (CPD) highlighted the significant achievements of the initiative and the policy interventions undertaken during the year. Dr. T. S. Rana, Head, CSIR-HRDC, Ghaziabad emphasized CSIR's commitment to transforming knowledge into digitally enabled, experiential, and innovation-driven solutions for skill development.
Dr. Mohana Krishna Reddy Mudiam, Director, Institute of Pesticide Formulation Technology (IPFT), Gurugram, and Chairman of the Monitoring Committee underscored that skill development is an integral part of nation-building and outlined five key priority pillars to guide the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative towards building a robust, future-ready, and industry-aligned skill development ecosystem. Dr. Ashish Lele, Director, CSIR-NCL, Pune emphasized that that CSIR is uniquely positioned to make a meaningful contribution to the Skill India Mission by leveraging its extensive nationwide laboratory network and scientific expertise to help position India as a global hub for skilled talent.
A major highlight of the conclave was the comprehensive review of the annual progress achieved during 2025–26 under Phase III of the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative. CSIR-NIScPR Conducted Two-day Skill Training Program on “Popular Science Writing” and Motivated Participants to Communicate Science to Layman
articles.full_content:
New Delhi, 8 August 2026: CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (NIScPR), New Delhi, successfully organised a two-day Skill Training Program on “Popular Science Writing” during 6–7 August 2026 under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III). The program aimed to strengthen the science communication and writing skills of researchers, academicians, scientists, students, IT professionals, and R&D personnel. A total of 21 participants from across the country attended the Program.
Dr. Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR addressing the participants of Popular Science Writing Traning Course
The Program was inaugurated by Dr. Geeta Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, who encouraged participants to communicate scientific research in a simple, accurate, and engaging manner to promote scientific temper and bridge the gap between science and society. Mr. Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR, welcomed the participants and highlighted the importance of popular science writing in enhancing the societal impact of scientific research. The Program was coordinated by Ms. Meetali Bharti, Nodal Principal Investigator, and Mr. Mohd. Salim Ansari, Co-Principal Investigator. Dr. Manish Mohan Gore, Course Coordinator, provided an overview of the Program and coordinated the academic sessions throughout the training.
The programme featured expert lectures and hands-on sessions delivered by eminent resource persons, including Ms. Neha Tripathi, who spoke on Basics of Popular Science Writing and Creative Formats; Dr. Bornali Sarma delivered a session on How to Write a Popular Science Story from a Research Article; Dr. Matiur Rahman discussed the Use of AI to Create Impactful Content for Social Media; NDTV’s Science Editor Shri Pallav Bagla, conducted a practical session on Science Writing for Digital Media; Dr. Meher Wan, Scientist-D explained the Skill of Writing Press Releases on Scientific Research and Events; and Dr. Manish Mohan Gore addressed the Ethical Aspects and Career Opportunities in Popular Science Writing. The program also included interactive discussions and hands-on exercises on various genres of popular science writing, enabling participants to gain practical experience in communicating science effectively. Participants appreciated the program's practical orientation and the opportunity to interact with experienced science communicators and media professionals. The training enhanced their understanding of effective science communication, digital content creation, and science writing for diverse audiences.
The Program concluded with a valedictory session, during which Mr. Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training addressed the participants and distributed certificates with the Program Team members. The successful completion of the program reaffirmed CSIR-NIScPR's commitment to developing skilled science communicators and promoting excellence in science communication through capacity-building initiatives under

articles.full_content:
Abdarpur, Birbhum, August 7, 2026
Press Information Bureau (PIB), Kolkata today organised a Vartalaap, the media workshop at Abdarpur, Birbhum, to strengthen awareness on major flagship initiatives of the Union Government, including Ayushman Bharat, Census 2027, Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Grameen) [VB-G RAM G] Act, 2025 and financial inclusion initiatives. The programme brought together Government officials, media representatives and stakeholders to facilitate dialogue on key public welfare initiatives and their effective dissemination among the citizens.
Addressing the gathering, Director General (East Zone), Press Information Bureau, Shri T. V. K. Reddy, underscored the growing importance of authentic information in the age of social media. He highlighted PIB's role in disseminating verified government information, translating, official content into regional languages and providing backgrounders to facilitate informed reporting. He also emphasised PIB's role during crisis communication, the significance of the PIB Fact Check initiative in combating misinformation and the importance of Vartalaap in connecting with grassroots journalists, addressing their queries and promoting effective development communication.
The Minister for Agriculture, Government of West Bengal, Shri Dudh Kumar Mondal inaugurated the workshop today. He highlighted the transformative potential of the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 in accelerating rural development and generating sustainable livelihoods. He also stressed the importance of efficient implementation of government schemes for improving the rural economy and underlined the need for easy access to institutional credit for farmers. He emphasised on the availability of fertilisers at Maximum Retail Price (MRP), promotion of modern agricultural technologies and expansion of irrigation infrastructure to enhance agricultural productivity.
Speaking on Ayushman Bharat, Chief Medical Officer of Health (CMOH), Birbhum, Dr. Subhabrata Ghosh, informed that 27.58 lakh beneficiaries in the district would be covered under the scheme. He announced that Ayushman Bharat card distribution would commence from August 16, while Ayushman Bharat Week would be observed from August 8 to 15, featuring health check-up camps, awareness rallies, marathons, school health camps and mobile health services. He also stressed the importance of HPV vaccination, urging people not to be misled by misinformation. 412 TH REPORT ON ‘FOREST FIRES IN THE HIMALAYAN REGION, ITS ADVERSE EFFECTS AND MITIGATION’
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS-AT A GLANCE
FOREST FIRES IN THE HIMALAYAN REGION: EXTENT AND TRENDS
The Committee desired to know as to whether any research has been undertaken on the linkage between climate change and increasing fire frequency in the Himalayan region and put a query to this effect to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. In response, the Ministry stated that it recognises that rising temperatures, prolonged dry spells and increasing climate variability are contributing factors to the increasing frequency and intensity of forest fire occurrence in the region. The Ministry, however, informed the Committee that no specific research study on this linkage has, as yet, been commissioned or assigned by the Ministry .
The Committee notes that there is no dedicated research study to establish or quantify that climate change is a contributing factor to the rising frequency and intensity of forest fires in the Himalayan region. The Committee takes note of the ongoing work under the NCSFFM at ICFRE-FRI; however, it observes that this work, being forward-looking and scenario-based in its design, is oriented towards projecting future fire vulnerability rather than towards empirically establishing the historical relationship between climate variables and past fire incidence. The Committee is, therefore, of the view that a knowledge gap persists in this regard, and that the Himalayan region, given its ecological fragility, topographic complexity and high sensitivity to climatic shifts, requires dedicated region-specific research rather than reliance on general or extrapolated findings from other forest ecosystems. (Para 2.20)
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should commission a dedicated, region-specific research study to establish the empirical linkage between climate change and forest fire frequency, intensity and seasonality in the Indian Himalayan Region. Such a study should, at a minimum, examine long-term trends in temperature, precipitation and dry-spell duration against historical forest fire incidence data; assess how altitudinal and species-wise variation across Himalayan forest types affects fire vulnerability under changing climatic conditions; and generate predictive fire-risk models that can inform s

No Proposal at Present to Establish Integrated Drug De-addiction and Vocational Training Centres in Jammu
articles.full_content:
Jammu & Kashmir Currently Has 1 IRCA, 6 District De-addiction Centres and 21 Addiction Treatment Facilities Under NAPDDR
The Government has informed the Rajya Sabha that there is no proposal at present to establish integrated drug de-addiction and vocational training centres in the Jammu region.
Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B.L. Verma , in a written reply to Shri Sat Paul Sharma in the Rajya Sabha, stated that the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir presently has one Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) and six District De-addiction Centres (DDACs) functioning as rehabilitation centres. Additionally, two Community-based Peer Led Intervention (CPLI) centres, three Outreach and Drop-In Centres (ODICs), and twenty-one Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) have been established under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) to strengthen de-addiction services in the Union Territory. The Minister further informed that the establishment and monitoring of new de-addiction centres is a continuous process.
Replying to a query regarding measures taken under the Narco Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism to tackle drug trafficking in Jammu & Kashmir, Shri Verma informed that the Ministry of Home Affairs has established a four-tier NCORD mechanism comprising Apex, Executive, State/UT and District-level committees to ensure better coordination among Central and State drug law enforcement agencies and other stakeholders engaged in combating drug trafficking and drug abuse.
The Minister further informed that 17 State-Level NCORD meetings and 836 District-Level NCORD meetings have been held in the Union Territory since 2018 to review the drug trafficking scenario, monitor enforcement actions and ensure timely implementation of decisions. The 10th Apex Level NCORD meeting was held on 26 June 2026 .
The House was also informed that the NCORD Portal serves as a comprehensive knowledge management platform for all four tiers of the NCORD mechanism. The portal functions as a repository of information relating to narcotics control and anti-drug abuse initiatives undertaken by the Central Government, thereby facilitating coordination and information sharing among all stakeholders.
The Government continues to strengthen institutional mechanisms for prevention, treatment and rehabilitation under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction while enhancing inter-agency coordination to effectively address the challenges posed by drug trafficking and substance abuse across the country.

articles.full_content:
Start-Ups To Receive Dedicated "Start-Up Badge" On Official Buyer Discovery Platform
In a major step towards promoting innovation-led exports and strengthening India's global trade ecosystem, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, has expanded the eligibility criteria for the "Source from India" service on the Trade Connect ePlatform to include eligible DPIIT-recognised Start-ups.
The decision, notified through a Trade Notice no. 16 dated August 06, 2026 issued today, aims to provide greater international visibility to India's growing start-up ecosystem by enabling innovative exporters to showcase their products and capabilities on the Government's official digital buyer discovery platform.
Trade Connect, launched by the Department of Commerce, serves as a one-stop digital interface connecting Indian exporters with trade-related services and institutional support. One of its flagship features, "Source from India," enables eligible exporters to create dedicated digital microsites that allow international buyers to discover reliable Indian suppliers and connect with them directly.
Under the revised framework, with effect from August 06, 2026, DPIIT-recognised Start-ups meeting the existing eligibility criteria under "Source from India" will be able to create their microsites on the platform and will be identified through a unique Start-up Badge, making them easily discoverable by overseas buyers.
Further, to encourage early-stage exporters, a special onboarding provision has also been introduced. DPIIT-recognised Start-ups possessing an active Import Export Code (IEC) that is not in the Denied Entity List (DEL) will also be eligible to create their profiles on "Source from India", even if they do not presently fulfil the standard export performance criteria. Their onboarding will be subject to verification through the DGFT IEC database.
The initiative is expected to significantly strengthen the participation of innovation-driven enterprises in international trade by providing them with enhanced visibility on an official Government platform. It is also expected to support export diversification, promote technology-led products and services, and reinforce India's emergence as a global hub for innovation and entrepreneurship.
Start-up users already registered on Trade Connect whose accounts are linked to eligible IECs will automatically receive the option to create their "Source from India" microsites from their dashboard. A detailed user guide has also been issued to facilitate seamless registration and profile creation.
The revised framework builds upon the earlier expansion of "Source from India", under which all valid IEC holders meeting the prescribed export realisation criteria became eligible to join the platform. By extending the initiative to India's start-up ecosystem, the Government seeks to create new opportunities for innovative enterprises to access global markets while further strengthening India's expo
